In South Asian societies, the moon is traditionally considered a symbol of peace, calmness, and purity, and is often associated with the feminine divine. The Islamic calendar is based on the lunar cycle, and the sighting of the new moon marks the beginning of a new month and the opportunity for a fresh start. Chandni's name implies a connection to this powerful and guiding celestial body, and may be seen as a reminder of the spiritual guidance and illumination that can be found in the natural world. Furthermore, in Sufi mysticism, the moon is sometimes used as a metaphor for the Divine Beloved, who illuminates and guides the heart. Chandni's name may thus also be seen as a reminder of the spiritual longing and yearning for the Divine that is at the heart of the human experience.
